findings.summary: The Apache License 2.0 is a permissive free-software license created by the Apache Software Foundation that allows users to freely use, distribute, and modify software. It permits combining code with GPLv3 projects, but contributions implicitly grant a patent license, and patent litigation against the work terminates that license. While widely adopted by major projects like Android, it is not considered free by OpenBSD due to its patent provisions and the involvement of contract law with copyright.

mechanisms.title: Permissive licensing and attribution
mechanisms.explanation: Users may use, distribute, and modify the software for any purpose without paying royalties. The license requires preserving copyright notices, disclaimers, and attribution in unmodified files. Modified files must include a notice that changes were made. A NOTICE file distributed with the work must retain third-party attributions, though these notices do not alter the license terms.

mechanisms.title: Patent license termination clause
mechanisms.explanation: Section 3 of the license grants users a patent license from contributors to make, use, sell, or import the work. However, if a user initiates patent litigation alleging that the software or a contribution infringes patents, any patent licenses granted under the license are automatically terminated for that work.

unknowns: How jurisdiction-specific contract law variations affect the predictability of license terms
Whether the patent license explicitly covers contributors' own patents beyond necessarily infringing ones
The exact scope of what constitutes a "contribution" that triggers the implicit patent grant
How the NOTICE file requirements interact with other attribution mechanisms in derivative works
